x: Haynes and B. Eglington were walking extremely well and Gordon Waddington was showing glimpses of his old form.

At 6½ miles, the two Georges, Oliver and Beecham, after their excellent County performances, were in 29th and 31st positions, with Hugh McGreechan 33rd, Garry Warr 38th, George Checkley 43rd, Percy Wright 44th, Harry Kemp 58th, Bob Readman 72nd, and Bernard Eglington 77th.
Alan Robins finished very well, just in tront of Bernard Eglington, who travelled up from Salisbury and, although suffering from a sprained ankle, completed the course well.
George Beecham was showing great form on his first 20 in third position, followed by Harry Shields, Norman Guilmant and Bernard Eglington, with the others coming along steadily.

We were pleased to have a team in this event and, ably led by Percy Wright, who finish 4th, we won the team race, with Norman Guilmant taking 1st and Bernard Eglington 3rd Handicap prizes, both reaping the reward of their consistent improvement.

We managed to enter a team in this event, in which Norman Guilmant showed that he is still improving, when he finished 2nd to Vic Stone. Backed up by Harry Shields, Bernard Eglington and Alan Robins, we managed to finish 2nd to Poly., being only 3 points behind.
Our other walkers, Bernard Eglington, Joe Wilson, Percy Wilson, all gave a good account of themselves. The usual enthusiastic support was in evidence and much appreciated by the walkers.

Our new members again showed up very well, Bob Newson renewing his tussle with Bernard Eglington and just getting the best of it. It was pleasing to see young Joe Scamell walking so well again and hope this will continue during the track season.

…ght, representing Southampton A.C., finished 4th and 6th respectively and gained first team medals. Last but not least, Bernard Eglington competed in the Wiltshire Championship and finished 3rd in 88.57.…

Syd James was second in the individual race in 85.56, followed by Norman Guilmant 4th,Bernard Eglington 6th and Harry Shields 10th, making a total of 20 points and 2nd place in the team race, to Trowbridge A.C.

…m - McGreechan Newson and Eglington - won the handicap team race, the "B" Team - Rolfe Wilson and Doubleday - were 2nd; Bernard Eglington (22.0) won the individual handicap, and Fred Rolfe (28.0) was 2nd in fact it is rumoured that the coach driver complained about the extra load on the way home, wh…

George Checkley was a good second in 2hrs. 58mins. 23secs., Bernard Eglington coming next nearly 7 minutes behind in 3hrs. 5mins. 14sec. Norman Guilmant, 4th, Bob Newson, 5th, George Beecham 6th and Fred Rolfe 7th all completed the course inside 3hrs. 15mins.

Bernard Eglington, 13th, missed his by one position. George Beecham gained his first National winning team medal, Hugh McGreechan the Sydney Bayliss Cup and Bob Newson his first (2nd Class) National Standard medal.
Hugh McGreechan was 3rd in the race, Norman Guilmant 5th, Bernard Eglington 9th and Harry Shields 10th, all inside 5 hours. In addition Harry took the second handicap prize and Norman the 3rd.
May I have many letters of acknowledgement to write, it will be a welcome task. Bernard Eglington was unfortunately sent abroad just a week before the Brighton Walk.
Hugh McGreechan was 4th with the leading bunch, Norman Guilmant, George Checkley, George Beecham, Harry Shields and Bernard Eglington, in that order, not far behind.
Hugh McGreechan, Bernard Eglington, George Checkley and Harry Shields - just a bare team - plus myself as general factotum, travelled up to Birmingham for this popular event.

As stated earlier, we were without Bernard Eglington, but nevertheless we started two teams, 8 and 4 respectively backed up by a swarm of supporters at Big Ben which increased considerably as we moved towards Brighton.

We were pleased to see Bernard Eglington on leave from Germany and how well he walked, clocking 58.14. We finished 4th in the handicap which gave us great hopes of success in our own Open a fortnight later.

Bernard Eglington, on his last days leave from Germany, took the prize for the first Belgrave member unplaced in the scratch events. Although it started raining towards the end, in fact the recording was done in heavy rain, everything went well and we owe a hearty vote of thanks to the officials on…
It was pleasing to see Bennard Eglington home from Germany and competing. From then on the race underwent rapid changes and our lads started to move up.

Next for us in 8th position was George Checkley, another grand performance and our scoring team was completed by Bob Newson, trying gallantly even in the last yard to catch and pass the Woodford man a pace ahead, and Bernard Eglington on leave from Germany.

Also a welcome home to Bernard Eglington who "wangled" leave for both this and the "National". Having retained our National 20 title and regained the Nijmegen Shield, we looked forward to the next big race, the 50 Kilos, with eager anticipation, but alas, owing to the unfortunate loss of Hugh McGree…

For this classic of all road races, it was very pleasing to have Bernard Eglington who flew home from Germany for the occasion. We were without George Checkley, who finished 7th last year, but nevertheless we started a full "A" team plus two individuals and were very hopeful of a successful day.
Bernard Eglington has not been so fortunate this year in getting home from Germany for the major championships, but we hope to see him on the Brighton.

Bernard Eglington home on leave from Germany, walked strongly to finish 4th in 3.45.40. George Beecham was 7th after overcoming a bad spell in 3.47.37 and Cyril Yescombe who was very strong over the second half, clocked his best time for the distance in 4.55.44.

Bernard Eglington, suffering from lack of a good breakfast started to come through well and at one time was in front of George Beecham and Harry Shields, but was unable to hold it and fell back again.
Bernard Eglington, back from service in Germany was always ready to step into the breach if needed and Cyril Yescombe maintained his progress.

Support, if necessary, was always at hand, for Cyril Yescombe scored 8th (actual 11th) and earns our hearty congratulations on gaining his Honours Badge; our sympathies to Bernard Eglington on missing his by one place.
In the Leicester Open '7' on October 6th, Eric Hall (55:31) was 7th and Bernard Eglington (61:51) 46th.
Although John Morris, Bernard Eglington, John Keown and Bob Farley fought hard to make up team places,this was to affect the team result considerably in the end.

Leading right from the start he went away steadily to win by a clear five minutes from Dennis Read of Steyning AC. Belgrave pipped their main rivals, Surrey WC., for the team event, thanks to fine support from Pat Duncan and Bernard Eglington.

Despite fine support from John Morris and Bernard Eglington we were obliged, however, to concede the team title to Surrey WC. The field included Gordon Hazle (Germiston Callies Harriers) the South African Champion, and Dennis Read (Steyning AC) the holder and brother of Norman Read the Rome Olympics gold medallist.
Greetings to all members come from Bernard Eglington now serving in Malta where between duties he is acting as "talent-spotter" for Belgrave.
John Keown walked steadily for third place while Bernard Eglington, fully acclimatised from his training in Malta, sneaked the handicap from F.Rolfe with Keown taking third prize.
Bernard Eglington, shortly to retire from the R.A.F. joined us as a runner but turned to walking and did very well. His service took him throughout the world and his Belgrave colours went with him.
Bernard Eglington was obviously tired after his trip from Wales. It was our fourth consecutive win, making some amends for defeat at the hands of Leicester and Basildon in the Enfield '7'.
Bernard Eglington made the long trip down from North Wales for the Belgrave Open '7'. Bob Picton showed just a little of what he could so easily be capable of in the Met.

The next "B and B" (1963) saw two Belgravians doing the journey stride by stride, Cyril Yescombe (another Police stalwart) who died tragically a few years ago and Bernard Eglington, former runner from Derby and R.A.F. man.

Finally came Pat Duncan, and although many of the walkers at the front went off faster than him he was unable to pull them back again when he began to "come through" with 20 yards to go. Bernard Eglington unfortunately arrived too late to start.

Congratulations to Vice-President BERNARD EGLINGTON upon his recent marriage. He joined the Club about thirty years ago when he was a full time member of the R.A.F., and was previously with Derby & County.
Bernard Eglington, who still shows the Claret and Gold on the beaches and roads of N.Wales, and of course pops down for the odd race. Frank Simmons, always full of training advice.

Leading the table of 'Brightons' successfully completed since the last war are John Keown with 16 (consecutive); George Beecham with 15; Joe Wilson, Harry Shields and Bernard Eglington with 12 each; Gordon Doubleday with 11 (2 before the war) and Johnny Morris and Dave King with 10 each.
He hopes to visit the U.K. in 1979 - give him a number Carl! Bernard Eglington informs us that he is retiring this year. He will be cutting down on his forays into Lancashire for the occasional spin.
We hear that Bernard Eglington pulled off the biggest fiddle of his athletic career in October. He has been walking second-claim with Lancs.
Bernard Eglington (13th) missed his by one position. George Beecham (17th) gained his first National winning team medal, Hugh McGreechan (4th) the Sidney Bayliss Cup.

Once again Belgrave showed that when the conditions get tough it is the other clubs who retire. 2, R.C.Middleton 4:33:28; 10, P.Duncan 4:53:32; 11, D.King 4:54:22; 42, J.Keown 5:33:58; 46, B.Eglington 5:37:53."
